channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Tech Titans, Trump Fete China’s Xi at State Dinner
item.description: Luminaries from Wall Street and Silicon Valley joined US President Donald Trump for a state dinner honoring his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping. Steve Engle reports from Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Former NSC China Director on Trump-Xi Summit
item.description: Liza Tobin, Former China Director at the US National Security Council and Managing Director of Garnaut Global, discusses her expectations and takeaways from the summit between Presidents Trump and Xi. She speaks with Haidi Stroud Watts on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade". (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hong Kong’s Buy&Ship Eyes Tokyo Listing In Japan Expansion Push
item.description: Buy&Ship is the first Hong Kong-based company chosen by the Tokyo Stock Exchange to join its initial public offering incubation program, giving it a hand in expanding its presence in Japan.
item.dc:creator: Yasutaka Tamura and Julia Fioretti

item.title: Australia Demands More AI Safeguards After Revealing OpenAI Hack
item.description: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese used his trip to the United Nations to call for greater controls on artificial intelligence, pointing to the revelation that OpenAI had hacked a government website as evidence of the need for tougher safeguards.
item.dc:creator: James Mayger

item.title: Goldman’s Moe Says He’s in ‘Stronger-for-Longer Camp’ on AI
item.description: Artificial intelligence-related stocks remain attractive despite rising government bond yields, Goldman Sachs Group Inc.’s Timothy Moe said.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Why US-China AI Talks Are About Risk Management
item.description: Former US official Sarah Beran contends that US-China AI engagement will center on risk reduction rather than deep collaboration. She highlights guardrails and threat-reporting channels as the primary realistic outcomes given the intense strategic competition between Washington and Beijing. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: FBI Agent Homes, Job Titles in Data Hackers Claim to Have Stolen
item.description: A trove of data that hackers say they stole from the Federal Bureau of Investigation includes records revealing the home addresses of employees involved in investigating foreign spies, drug cartels and running covert surveillance operations.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gallagher and Jake Bleiberg

item.title: US Treasury Yields Hit 5% as Wall Street Faces New Rate Regime
item.description: As yields on US Treasuries soar past one high after the next, a reality is sinking in deeper across Wall Street and Washington: More than merely a bond-market slump, this might just be a fundamental shift.
item.dc:creator: Michael MacKenzie and Enda Curran

item.title: US-China Rivalry Fuels Fierce AI Race: Live Q&A
item.description: Bloomberg journalists answer your questions about the fierce US-China AI race in a Live Q&A on Friday, Sept. 25 at 9 a.m. EDT // 9 p.m. HKT
item.dc:creator: Stephen Engle, Michael Shepard, Nectar Gan and Henry Ren

item.title: Oil, Treasury Yields & Inflation Pressure Markets
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are MSCI Chairman & CEO Henry Fernandez, NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, Apple Store Creator Ron Johnson, Principal Asset Management CIO George Maris, Pictet Research Institute Head Maria Vassalou, BlackRock Portfolio Manager, Global Fixed Income Investment Group Chi Chen, Whole Foods CEO & Amazon Worldwide Grocery Stores Vice President Jason Buechel, ALDI US Chief Operating Officer Dave Rinaldo, & Global Citizen CEO Hugh Evans. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Store Creator on New Book and Retail’s AI Future
item.description: Ron Johnson, Creator of the Apple Store and author of the new book "Shop Different: How Retail Revealed Apple's Genius" takes a look at the strategy behind the iconic Apple Store and how Apple has transformed over more than 50 years. He begins by reflecting on the long-running debate over whether the internet would kill retail, suggesting that concern was overstated. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Sally Bakewell on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Live Nation Has Received $420 Million in Subsidies From US Cities: Study
item.description: A new report digs into the subsidies that local governments provide the entertainment giant
item.dc:creator: Ashley Carman

item.title: MSCI CEO: Investors Are Putting Money Everywhere
item.description: Henry Fernandez, Chairman and CEO at MSCI, discusses Oracle’s force majeure notice in the context of heavy borrowing and large investments tied to the long-term AI story. He goes on to talk about global inflation that may linger and the Fed may need to hike again, framing the segment around pressure in markets and the cost of capital. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Sally Bakewell on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Goldman Sachs Is Underweight Hyperscalers on Debt Supply Surge
item.description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc.’s Lindsay Rosner says the bank’s asset management arm is underweight on the biggest artificial intelligence borrowers as a flood of issuance washes over the market.
item.dc:creator: Zahra Tayeb

item.title: Maria Vassalou on Rising Government Debt, Trump-XI Summit
item.description: Maria Vassalou, Head of the Pictet Research Institute, discusses the deepening global bond rout and Treasury market pressure. She goes on to talk about the growing talk of a U.S. debt reckoning is being overstated too soon, setting up a broader conversation about whether current market concerns are getting ahead of the underlying economic reality. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Principal CIO on Inflation Concerns, Rising Bond Yields
item.description: George Maris of Principal Asset Management discusses the growing pressure on equities from the bond market. The conversation focuses on whether the recent rise in yields, both overall and in terms of the speed of the move over the past few months, has reached a level where stock investors should be increasingly concerned. He speaks to Romaine Bostick & Sally Bakewell on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Biology Lab Enzyme Discovery Draws Caution From Scientists
item.description: Anthropic PBC’s announcement that its Claude AI model discovered an enzyme system that resembled an earlier breakthrough gene editing technology was met with caution by some experts in the field, who suggested the company oversold its significance.
item.dc:creator: Robert Langreth

item.title: Odd Lots: Maybe AI Won’t Kill Us All — Just Some of Us
item.description:
Big Tech has been sounding alarms about the risk of AI causing human extinction but there are also skeptics who dismiss the notion, like former US Federal Trade Commissioner Alvaro Bedoya, who referenced the Black Death to dismiss warnings of existential risks.
On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast recorded live at the Vermont Hollywood theater, Rachel Karten, author of the Link in Bio newsletter, and Taylor Lorenz, founder of User Mag, talk about the possibility of AI killing all humans, or maybe just some. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Strikes $12 Billion AI Computing Deal With Akamai
item.description: Anthropic PBC has signed an $11.6 billion, seven-year contract with Akamai Technologies Inc. for computing power, adding to the AI developer’s growing list of data center deals.
item.dc:creator: Lynn Doan

item.title: Indonesia Court Cuts Nadiem Makarim Term in Graft Appeal
item.description: An Indonesian appeals court upheld the corruption conviction of former Education Minister and Gojek co-founder Nadiem Makarim but cut his 10-year prison sentence to nine years.
item.dc:creator: Chandra Asmara
